questions.question: Before riding, check your motorcycle clutch. A clutch that works properly should feel:

options.text: Loose and rough.
Tight and smooth.
Loose and smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tight and smooth.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your clutch and throttle. The throttle should snap back when you release it. The clutch should feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: When riding at night, what should you do?

options.text: Ride on the shoulder of the road.
Stay closer to the vehicle in front of you.
Stay farther away from the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther away from the vehicle in front of you.
questions.explanation: At night, increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Slow down and adjust your lane position as needed.

questions.question: When a driver makes eye contact with you:

options.text: It means they see you.
It will never happen.
It does not mean they will let you go first.
It guarantees they will let you go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean they will let you go first.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact to know a driver will let you go first. Drivers often look at motorcyclists but do not actually see them.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance when:

options.text: The road is wet or slippery.
The sun is shining.
You can stop normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is wet or slippery.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle will take longer to stop. Examples include wet roads, when you cannot see past the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy and another driver might cut in front of you.

questions.question: If you see a hazard ahead, you should:

options.text: Not talk to other drivers about it.
Change your speed.
Use your horn, lights, or signals to warn others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not talk to other drivers about it.
questions.explanation: To avoid a hazard, warn other drivers by using your horn, lights, and signals. Adjust your speed and change your lane position as needed.

questions.question: Riding right next to another vehicle is dangerous because:

options.text: The vehicle may block your way to escape.
Other drivers can easily see you.
You cannot read road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle may block your way to escape.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is risky. The vehicle could move into your lane and hit you. It could also block your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: Oil and road debris usually collect in which part of a lane?

options.text: The left side
The center
The right side

questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: Oil drips and debris from vehicles build up in the center of a lane.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle in a curve?

options.text: The outside edge
The inside edge
Wherever traffic and road conditions allow

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever traffic and road conditions allow
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Choose a lane position that fits the conditions and adjust as you go.

questions.question: Which is NOT a benefit of staying away from other vehicles?

options.text: You have more time to react to other drivers.
You have room to move safely.
You have few ways to escape.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have few ways to escape.
questions.explanation: Keeping space between you and other vehicles gives you time to react and room to move safely.

questions.question: If you must ride over an obstacle, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up before you hit it.
Stay seated for cushioning.
Hit it at a 90-degree angle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hit it at a 90-degree angle.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, slow down and hit it as straight on as possible, close to a 90-degree angle.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait for the emergency vehicle to start moving.
Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside help stopped with flashing lights, you must change lanes to give it extra space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You will have time to react to hazards.
You will have space to change direction.
You will have more time to speed up when entering a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have more time to speed up when entering a curve.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle helps you react faster and move out of danger if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: When passing a truck on a two-lane road, when should you return to your lane?

options.text: When you can see the front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
As soon as the truck is behind you.
When you think you have enough space.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Return to your lane only when you can see the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: What does a solid white line on the edge of the road mean?

options.text: Parking is not allowed.
The right edge of a traffic lane.
Traffic must merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the road edge marks the right side of a traffic lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead
Yield
Reduce speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black symbols. This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is coming up.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what should you do on your motorcycle?

options.text: Leave the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
Ride in the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When it rains, do not ride in the center of the lane. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by other cars. The left tire track is usually the safest, but this depends on traffic.

questions.question: ________ of motorcycle and car crashes happen because the car driver did not yield to the motorcyclist.

options.text: One-quarter
More than half
One-half

questions.correctAnswerText: More than half
questions.explanation: More than half of crashes between motorcycles and cars happen because drivers fail to yield to motorcyclists. Never assume that larger vehicles will yield to you, even if they should.

questions.question: You reach an intersection with no signs or signals at the same time as another vehicle. What should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlights to tell the other vehicle to go.
Go through the intersection and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what is the best place to ride your motorcycle?

options.text: In the center of the lane.
In the tire tracks left by cars.
On the side of the road until the rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When it rains, the oily center of the lane is very slippery. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars instead. The left tire track is often safest, but this can vary.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop completely and go when it is safe.
Only stop if other traffic is coming.
Vehicles will be entering the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely, let all traffic and people pass, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What color are service signs?

options.text: Orange with black letters.
Blue with white letters.
Green with white letters.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blue with white letters.
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. Services include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride under the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Speed up before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: When approaching a dangerous area like an intersection, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to hazards.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
The rear brake is more powerful than the front brake.
Both brakes are equally powerful.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of your motorcycle's stopping power.

questions.question: What separates lanes moving in the same direction?

options.text: White lines.
Yellow lines.
Road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed white lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: When you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do both actions at the same time.
Only brake.
Do one action, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: When you must swerve and brake, do them separately. Brake then swerve, or swerve then brake. Do not do both at the same time.

questions.question: The center of a lane has an oily strip. What about this strip?

options.text: You should avoid it at all times.
It usually gives good grip, unless it is raining.
You should only ride on it when sharing the lane with another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It usually gives good grip, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The oily strip usually provides enough grip for safe riding, except when it is raining. The strip is usually only about two feet wide, so you can ride on either side of it and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: When a vehicle is passing you from behind, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: Right side
Center
Left side

questions.correctAnswerText: Center
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases the risk of a crash. Riding on the far side may make the driver return to your lane unsafely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You may go through with caution.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. You must stop completely and wait for a signal that allows you to turn.

questions.question: Where do most motorcycle and car crashes happen?

options.text: At intersections.
On open roads.
In parking lots.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections.
questions.explanation: Most crashes between motorcycles and cars happen at intersections. The main cause is drivers failing to give the right-of-way to motorcyclists.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Ride slower than usual.
Allow more distance to stop than usual.
Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.
questions.explanation: With a passenger, your motorcycle handles differently due to extra weight. Ride slower and allow more stopping distance. Your passenger should hold the passenger handgrips or your waist or hips, not the back of the bike.
